kjv: though I intreated for the children's [sake] of mine own body
mine: and I am a stench to the children of my own mother
note: hannoti is from hnn II "be loathsome" (parallel "my breath is strange"), and bene bitni are "the sons of my womb", i.e. of the womb that bore me, his brothers; the KJV takes hnn I "plead" and makes them Job's own children (who are dead, 1:19).

kjv: he shall stand at the latter [day] upon the earth
mine: at the last he will stand upon the dust
note: we'aharon is adverbial "at the last" or a title "as the Last/Afterward one"; the KJV's italic "day" makes it the eschatological Last Day, and 'afar "dust" may also be the grave.

kjv: And [though] after my skin [worms] destroy this [body], yet in my flesh shall I see God
mine: And after my skin has been thus destroyed, yet from my flesh I shall see God
note: the Hebrew has no "worms" or "body" (both KJV italics), and mibbesari can mean "from (within) my flesh", i.e. still embodied, or "apart from my flesh"; the KJV commits the verse to a bodily-resurrection reading that the Hebrew allows but does not state. Context: seeing God bodily ('from my flesh') (medium confidence). 19:27 'my eyes shall behold, and not another' stresses embodied sight. Whether this is after death or a vindication before death remains open.
